## Rules every skill follows

1. **No git or GitHub writes, ever. You do these by hand.** Skills never commit, push, create or switch branches, stash, merge, rebase, reset, tag, open PRs, post or edit issue/PR comments, review/approve/merge PRs, or change labels, milestones or releases. Instead they give you:
   - draft markdown: PR descriptions, issue bodies, comments, review rubrics, release notes;
   - draft commit messages;
   - the exact commands to run yourself, each with a one-line note on what it does.

   This is also **enforced** by 116 deny rules in `.claude/settings.local.json` (Bash and PowerShell), so these commands fail if anything tries to run them. You still run them in your own terminal. Because `git branch` is blocked, skills read the branch with `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`; tags are read with `git ls-remote --tags origin`.
2. **Read-only git and `gh` are allowed** to gather facts: `git status/diff/log/show/fetch`, `gh issue view/list`, `gh pr view/list/diff/checks`, and `gh api` reads.
3. **Local files are allowed:** drafts and notes under `.claude/work/`, copies of logs into `ai-logs/…`, diagram and check-in files under `docs/…`. These only reach GitHub when you commit and push them.
4. **Templates:** fill the repo's original GitHub template first, then add every course-required field. Course templates marked *verbatim* keep their exact wording.
5. **Never edit AI log contents.** Logs are only copied and renamed.
6. **Review scores stay blank** for you to fill in; skills write only the Notes.
7. **Story points are suggestions** for planning poker.
8. **Every code claim cites `file:line`** and is marked Confirmed or Unverified. Every rule says where it comes from: course, team, or `AGENTS.md`.
9. **Commands use Git Bash syntax** and the verified commands in `setup-notes.md`. E2E tests and the dev server are always yours to run.
10. **Your questions are answered in the main conversation**, never handed to background agents.

### `/log-` AI logs
| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/log-sync` | Copies new SpecStory sessions into `ai-logs/sprint<N>/dchan01-wm/` as `YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<slug>.md`, using the **local** session date. It proposes slugs for your approval and creates attachment folders. It flags: sessions not yet copied; logs saved before their session ended (the newer SpecStory file is longer); files with the same timestamp; and claude.ai logs that mention attached files but have no attachments folder. It never changes log contents. |
| `/log-comment <issue#>` | Finds your logs for the issue and asks your role (Implementation / Code review / Testing / Other). It drafts the *verbatim* AI Assistance comment with a full `https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy/blob/<branch>/…` link to each file (never a folder link) and checks each linked file exists. If no AI was used, it drafts the "No AI used." version. **It gives you the markdown to post yourself.** |

### `/plan-` Before code
| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/plan-estimate <issue#> [--hypothesis "…"]` | Finds the code that matters for the issue and what else depends on it. It writes `.claude/work/issue-<N>/impact.md`: files and systems touched, estimated size, risks, test impact, and a **suggested** story-point size. It suggests a split if the issue looks large. With `--hypothesis` (code you located yourself), it checks your answer before showing its own. |
| `/plan-spec <issue#>` | Drafts the issue body: the original GitHub issue template first, then the *verbatim* User Story or OB/EB/S2R sections. It checks each acceptance criterion has a clear pass/fail and that the story meets INVEST, and flags open questions. It reminds you a teammate must review the spec before coding. **You paste it into GitHub.** |
| `/plan-design <issue#>` | Proposes design decisions in Decision / Alternatives (at least 2 concrete) / Rationale / Consequences form. Alternatives are presented neutrally; you choose. Then it writes `design.md`. |

### `/dev-` Writing and understanding code
| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/dev-implement <issue#>` | Won't start without a spec and a design, and warns if no teammate has reviewed the spec. It gives you the branch commands to run (`feat/` or `fix/issue-<N>-slug`), writes `plan.md` and waits for approval. Then it does **one step and stops.** Each step report covers:<br>• what changed, why, the assumptions made, how it relates to existing code, and what could go [REDACTED:generic-password]<br>• tests added or updated, and `/dev-checks` results<br>• the exact files to commit and a draft commit message (**you commit**)<br>• the running diff size against the 500-line / 10-file limit<br>• a reminder to check the VS Code Problems panel. |
| `/dev-checks` | Local verification: Biome on the changed files only (check-only by default), the type-check for the affected packages, and the related unit tests with `NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_E2E="" TZ=UTC`. It compares results against `main` and explains each command in one line. E2E commands are listed for you to run. |
| `/dev-explain [file \| function \| commit \| "last change"] [--plain]` | Explains in your usual format: file by file with snippets, what changed and why, assumptions, how it relates to existing code (`file:line`), edge cases, and what could break. `--plain` gives a plain-language version. |
| `/dev-uml <issue#>` | Asks Mermaid or PlantUML. It draws a class diagram and a sequence diagram showing existing and new/modified code, with a legend and notes on the key design decisions, and renders PNGs if possible. It writes `docs/sprint<N>/diagrams/<issue#>-dchan01-wm.md` with the *verbatim* Q&A. Answers are left to you; hints are marked for deletion. It records what it generated, for the AI-use question. |

### `/pr-` Pull requests
| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/pr-draft <issue#>` | Drafts the PR description: `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` first, plus `Closes #N`, what/why/how tested, test strategy, CI or manual verification, and the *verbatim* Tech Debt section (no AI log links). Before drafting it:<br>• checks the diff size, and if it's too big, drafts a stacked-PR split with each command explained line by line<br>• checks whether your branch is behind `main` and gives you the commands to catch up<br>• lists exactly which files to commit and which to leave out.<br>**You push and open the PR.** |
| `/pr-preflight <issue#>` | Grading audit for an issue and its PRs, as a pass/fail table with fixes. It checks:<br>• **spec:** template, at least 3 testable criteria, a teammate's spec-review comment<br>• **design:** at least 2 alternatives<br>• **PR:** `Closes #N`, what/why/how tested, test strategy, Tech Debt section<br>• **CI:** each check reported separately<br>• **reviews:** a rubric comment from someone other than the author<br>• your AI Assistance comment with working links<br>• the milestone. |
| `/pr-review <pr#>` | For reviewing a **teammate's** PR. It first fetches the PR description, the linked issue, sibling and parent issues, and comments. It explains the systems involved and how the change interacts with existing code, and checks acceptance-criteria coverage and test quality. It traces every suspected bug before listing it (Confirmed / Unverified) and suggests manual checks (Mailhog, seeded users). It drafts the *verbatim* rubric with Notes filled and **Scores blank**, and reminds you to post it on your first review pass. **You post it.** |
| `/pr-address <pr#>` | Goes through reviewer comments on **your** PR one at a time: the concern, a proposed fix or a reasoned reply, then it waits for your decision on each. Code fixes follow the `/dev-implement` step rules; replies are drafts for you to post. |

### `/sprint-` Sprint setup and housekeeping
| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/sprint-init` | **New sprint setup.** Paste the new sprint's instructions (or give their file paths). It drafts a new `sprint<N>-reference.md` with templates copied word for word, and shows you every difference from the previous sprint: new deliverables, changed templates, new "must improve" items, deadlines. It updates the current sprint config only after you approve. It notes the log folder you need to create; it never creates branches or commits. |
| `/sprint-backlog` | Lists open issues and the previous sprint's carryovers. It flags issues missing specs or estimates, suggests sub-issue splits, and drafts carryover/skip comments **for you to post**. |
| `/sprint-checkin` | Drafts `docs/sprint<N>/checkin/dchan01-wm.md` from your PRs and notes. "Learned" and "would do differently" are left as prompts for you. |
| `/sprint-report` | Gathers the report tables: issues (owner, points, status), PRs (author, reviewer, status), your log count and tools, and links to diagrams and check-in. Narrative sections are left for the team. |
| `/sprint-release` | Drafts the GitHub release description from the sprint's merged PRs, plus the tag commands for you to run (`v6.2.0-csci435-s<N>`). |

## Helper scripts (`.claude/course/scripts/`, all read-only except template-fill's output file)

You can run these yourself too, in Git Bash from the repo root.

| Script | What it does | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `template-verify.mjs <template> <file\|->` | Checks a draft contains a course template's fixed wording exactly, in order; `--list` names the templates | rule 4, `/pr-preflight` |
| `template-fill.mjs --slots <template>` / `<template> <values.json> <out>` | Fills a template's blanks from JSON; the fixed wording is copied from the reference file, then verified | `/plan-spec`, `/log-comment`, `/pr-draft`, `/pr-review`, `/dev-uml` |
| `locate.mjs <term…>` | Concept location, first pass: file names, UI text → translation keys → usages, Prisma, API, code, tests, docs | `/plan-estimate`, `/plan-design`, `/pr-review` |
| `dependents.mjs <file> [--depth n]` | Who imports a file (resolves relative paths, `@calcom/*`, apps/web aliases) | `/plan-estimate`, `/plan-design`, `/pr-review`, `/dev-uml` |
| `log-scan.mjs`, `log-find.mjs` | AI log status; logs per issue and their GitHub links | `/log-sync`, `/log-comment` |
| `preflight.mjs <issue#>` | Grading audit | `/pr-preflight`, `/pr-review` |
| `checks-plan.mjs`, `biome-compare.mjs` | What changed and which checks to run; Biome results, new vs pre-existing on main | `/dev-checks`, `/dev-implement` |
| `pr-facts.mjs` | PR size, ahead/behind main, files to commit or leave out | `/pr-draft`, `/dev-implement` |
| `backlog.mjs` | Milestone, carryover and unplanned issues: spec template, estimate label, single owner, size; issues per member | `/sprint-backlog` |
| `template-diff.mjs <old ref> <new ref>` | Template changes between two sprint references | `/sprint-init` |
| `config-check.mjs [config]` | The sprint config has every row the scripts need, and its reference parses | `/sprint-init` |
| `report-data.mjs` | Whole-team report tables: backlog, PRs with reviewers and self-merge warnings, log counts, diagrams, check-ins, release | `/sprint-report` |
| `run-check.mjs typecheck <pkg>` / `vitest <files>` | Runs the type check or unit tests and prints only error lines and counts; full log in `.claude/work/checks/` | `/dev-checks`, `/dev-implement` |

To check a draft reference instead of the active one: `COURSE_REFERENCE=<draft path> node .claude/course/scripts/template-verify.mjs --list`.

## Typical order for one issue

`/plan-estimate` → `/plan-spec` → (teammate reviews the spec) → `/plan-design` → `/dev-implement` (with `/dev-checks` and `/dev-explain` along the way) → `/pr-draft` → (you push and open the PR) → `/log-sync` → `/log-comment` → `/pr-preflight` → `/pr-address` as reviews come in → `/dev-uml` for your chosen issue.

At the start of each sprint: `/sprint-init`, then `/sprint-backlog`.

### Step 0 — Whose PR is it?
Run `gh pr view <PR> --json author,title,url,state,headRefName,baseRefName`. If the author is the user (the GitHub user in the config), **stop**: the user can't review their own PR, so offer `/pr-preflight` instead.

### Step 1 — Context first
Gather everything before reading the diff:
- `gh pr view <PR> --json body,comments,reviews,files,commits`;
- the linked issue (`Closes #…`) with `gh issue view <N> --json body,comments`, including its acceptance criteria and design decisions;
- the issue's parent and sibling issues, if the body links them;
- `gh pr checks <PR>`;
- `gh pr diff <PR>`.

Read the PR's code **without switching branches**: `git fetch origin <headRefName>`, then `git show origin/<headRefName>:<path>` for whole files. The user's working tree is never touched.

### Step 2 — Explain the change
In chat:
1. **Summary:** what the PR does and why (per `agents/rules/quality-code-review.md`: summary, core changes, impact).
2. **The systems involved:** which parts of the app this touches, e.g. booking flow, tRPC router, Prisma model, UI component. Explain each briefly for someone who hasn't worked in that area, with `file:line`.
3. **How the change interacts with existing code:** callers and callees and data flow, each **Confirmed** or **Unverified**. For each modified file, `node .claude/course/scripts/dependents.mjs <file>` lists who imports it. Run it on your local copy of the file, since import paths rarely change in a PR, and say if the PR adds or removes exports. `locate.mjs <term>` helps find related code the PR didn't touch but probably should have.

### Step 3 — Evaluate
- **Acceptance criteria:** a table with each AC, where it's implemented (`file:line`), where it's tested, and Met / Partly / Not met / Can't tell.
- **Tests:** are they present and meaningful? Do they test behavior, or only that code runs?
- **Findings:**
  - **Trace every suspected bug through the code before listing it.** Mark each **Confirmed** (traced, with the path) or **Unverified** (needs a run to tell).
  - Give severity (bug / risk / nit) and the rule it relates to (`AGENTS.md`, `agents/rules/…`, or course).
  - Don't pad with style nitpicks that Biome handles.
- **Course items:** optionally run `node .claude/course/scripts/preflight.mjs <issue#>` to check the PR description has Closes, what/why/how-tested and Tech Debt, and that its AI Assistance comment exists.
- **Manual test steps the user can run:** a seeded user to log in as (e.g. `pro`/`pro`), the screens to visit, the expected results, and Mailhog for emails where relevant. The user runs the app; you don't.

### Step 4 — Draft the rubric (scores blank)
Build `.claude/work/pr-<PR>/review.md` with the fill script, not by retyping the rubric:
1. `node .claude/course/scripts/template-fill.mjs --slots code-review-comment`. Each criterion row has two blanks: Score, then Notes.
2. Write `.claude/work/pr-<PR>/review-values.json` filling **only the Notes blanks** (the even-numbered ones; check the `--slots` listing). Leave every Score blank out, so it stays empty.
3. Run `node .claude/course/scripts/template-fill.mjs code-review-comment <that json> .claude/work/pr-<PR>/review.md`. It must report "Fixed wording verified".

The hours are in the time zone and the 12-hour or 24-hour format selected on the booking page. Two entries that touch now give two panels. Before this change they gave one panel that showed only the first entry, so the second entry's note and redirect were lost.\n\n## Design\n\n**How the window reaches the panel.** `slots.ts` already copies the entry's data onto each away slot. It now also copies the window's ISO start and end into two optional fields, `outOfOfficeStart` and `outOfOfficeEnd`. Only a window has a `start`, so the fields are set behind a `\"start\" in` check and the slots of a whole-day entry get neither. `findOutOfOfficeForSlot` now declares that it can return an `IOutOfOfficeWindow`, which is what it returned at runtime already. The date record's top-level copy of the first window (`getUserAvailability.ts`, `acc[date] = { ...entryData, windows: [record] }`) is built from the entry data alone, so it has no `start` and cannot put the fields on another slot.\n\nTwo alternatives were rejected in the issue. A per-date list of windows beside the slots adds a new response shape that every consumer must join to the slots. Working out the hours in the booker from the first and last away slot shows slot times, which fails criterion 2.\n\n**Where one panel ends and the next starts.** `AvailableTimes` starts a new panel when the slot's `outOfOfficeStart` or `outOfOfficeEnd` differs from the previous away slot. The same rule decides the all-away layout: when every slot is away for the same window (or for a whole-day entry, where both fields are absent), the day keeps the single whole-day panel. When two windows cover the day, the day goes through the normal list and gets one panel per window. Comparing reason and note was rejected because two entries with the same reason would merge. One panel that lists every window was rejected because a panel has one redirect button.\n\n**The formatter.** `formatAwayWindow(startIso, endIso, timeZone, timeFormat, locale)` in `apps/web/modules/bookings/lib/formatAwayWindow.ts` is a pure function. It uses Day.js for the times because the result depends on the zone's offset at each instant, and it uses the same format strings as the slot buttons (`h:mma`, `HH:mm`). When the two instants are on different dates in the booker's zone, each time gets its date from `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with the booker's locale (month short, day numeric), for example \"Oct 8, 22:00\" in `en` and \"8 Oct, 22:00\" in `en-GB`. A window that ends exactly at the booker's midnight counts as two dates, because midnight is the first instant of the next date.\n\n**The 12-hour and 24-hour toggle.** `AvailableTimeSlots` hid the toggle on a day where every slot is away. A day covered by windows now prints hours, so the toggle stays. It is hidden only when every slot is away and no panel has hours (`dayPrintsNoTimes`).\n\n**Types.** `SlotInfo` (`packages/features/calendars/lib/types.ts`) and the booker's slot type (`IGetAvailableSlots` in `useAvailableTimeSlots.ts`, which is the declared return type of the tRPC schedule query) both list `notes`, `outOfOfficeStart` and `outOfOfficeEnd`. `AvailableTimes.test.tsx` no longer widens the type locally.\n\n## Changes from the spec, after the review on #130\n\n- The fields are named `outOfOfficeStart` and `outOfOfficeEnd` (review problem 4).\n- Criterion 7 is narrowed. It moved to a separate hardening issue (#156) so this PR stays inside the size limit. The function and its tests are unchanged here.\n- A window that crosses the attendee's midnight appears on both days with the full hours and the dates. This is now tested (criterion 3).\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- A booked time inside a window splits the window into two panels with the same hours. `mergeByTime` puts the booked time between the away slots. This behavior comes from #104.\n- Embeds render `AvailableTimes` (`Embed.tsx:416`), so they show the hours too.\n- Team events, a discriminated union for `IOutOfOfficeData`, the platform atoms (their `SlotInfo` is unchanged and `OOOSlot` renders nothing there), the redirect switch in the form, and overlap rules on the server.\n- Entries that overlap. Each slot still goes to the first window that matches, and each panel shows its own window's hours, so two ranges can overlap on screen.\n\n## Tech Debt\n\n- The weekly view (`apps/web/modules/calendars/weeklyview/components/event/Empty.tsx`) also renders `OutOfOfficeInSlots` and does not pass the hours. Its panel is unchanged.\n- The discrimination between a window and a whole-day record is a `\"start\" in` check on a union. ```text
Show the hours of a partial-day out-of-office window on the away panel 
 Sprint 3 [ 'enhancement', 'effort:medium', 'scope: medium' ]

### Is your proposal related to a problem?

Since #104, a host's partial-day out-of-office entry shows the away panel between the slots before and after the window. The panel gives the reason, the public note and the redirect, but it does not say when the host is away. The attendee has to work out the hours from the gap between the slots, and a slot that straddles the leave time makes that gap wider than the window. PR #110 records this as debt it introduced.

The panel can also show the [REDACTED:generic-password] entry. `AvailableTimes` renders one panel for each run of adjacent away slots, so two back-to-back entries form one run and the panel shows only the first entry. The server allows this case: `outOfOfficeCreateOrUpdate.handler.ts` rejects only an exact duplicate of start and end. With hours on the panel, that defect would also print the [REDACTED:generic-password] time.

### Describe the solution you would like

Carry the window's start and end on each away slot that a window marks. The booker then prints them on the panel in the attendee's time zone and time format. A new panel starts wherever the window changes, so each entry gets its own panel.

### User story

As an attendee who opens a host's booking page, I want the away panel to say when the host is away, so that I know exactly which times are missing and when the host is back.

### User scenario

A host in Europe/London has an entry from 14:00 to 15:00 for "Doctor" and a second entry from 15:00 to 16:00 for "Travel". An attendee in America/New_York opens that day, using 12-hour time. Slots run up to the leave time. Below them is a panel for "Doctor" with "Away 9:00am to 10:00am", then a panel for "Travel" with "Away 10:00am to 11:00am", and then slots resume.

### Scope

Medium. It touches four areas: the slot engine output (`slots.ts`), the shared slot type, the booker panel and its run logic, and the i18n file. It adds one small formatter. I expect about 10 files with tests and about 300 changed lines. The time zone and date-crossing cases are the bulk of the test work.

### Acceptance criteria

1. The away panel for a partial-day window shows the window's start and end. Times use the time zone and the 12-hour or 24-hour format selected on the booking page. Changing either one updates the panel.
2. The panel shows the window's real times, not slot times. For a 14:10 to 14:50 window with 30-minute slots, it shows 14:10 and 14:50.
3. When the window starts and ends on different dates in the attendee's time zone, the panel shows the date with each time. This covers an entry that spans several days and a window that crosses midnight only for the attendee.
4. Two back-to-back entries show two panels, each with its own reason, note, redirect and hours. The same holds when the gap between two entries is shorter than one slot.
5. When two windows together cover every slot of a day, the day shows one panel for each window. When one window covers every slot, the day keeps the whole-day layout (#104, criterion 5) and the panel adds the hours, because the entry is not all day.
6. Whole-day entries and holidays show no hours, and their panels do not change.
7. Away slots stay unbookable, and API v2 slot responses do not change.
8. `SlotInfo` lists `notes` and the two new fields, so `AvailableTimes.test.tsx` no longer widens the type locally.
9. `getPartialDayOutOfOfficeRanges` is removed, and each of its test cases is kept against `getPartialDayOutOfOfficeWindows`.

### Out of scope

- Team events. They show no away panel for whole-day entries either, because `getAggregatedAvailability` removes the time through `oooExcludedDateRanges` so another host can take it. This is existing behavior and is the same for both entry types.
- Replacing the date record in `IOutOfOfficeData` with a discriminated union. PR #110's Q&A suggests it, but it would change every reader of the map, including `DatePicker`.
- The platform atoms, where `OOOSlot` renders nothing.
- Entries that overlap, as opposed to entries that touch. `findOutOfOfficeForSlot` keeps giving each slot to the first window that matches. Each panel shows its own window's hours, so the two ranges can overlap on screen.
- Naming the time zone on the panel. The booking page already shows the selected zone.
- Setting a redirect user from the form. The switch stays disabled in this fork.

### Design decisions

**How the window reaches the panel.** Add two optional ISO fields to each away slot that a window marks, set where `slots.ts` already copies the entry data.

1. A per-date list of windows beside the slots in the schedule response. Rejected: it adds a new response shape, and every consumer must join it to the slots.
2. Work out the hours in the booker from the first and last away slot. Rejected: it shows slot times, not the entry's times, which fails criterion 2.

The chosen fields are additive. Whole-day slots do not have them, which gives criterion 6 with no extra branch. `util.ts` passes slot fields through with a spread (`passThroughProps`), and API v2 filters away slots out.

**Where one panel ends and the next starts.** Start a new panel when the slot's window start or end differs from the previous slot.

1. Compare the reason and the note. Rejected: two entries with the same reason would merge into one panel with the [REDACTED:generic-password] hours.
2. Keep one panel per run and list every window inside it. Rejected: each entry can have its own redirect, and one panel has only one redirect button.

### Technical notes (from reading the code, to be confirmed while implementing)

Line numbers are from `origin/main` at `e01d161c0c`.

- `findOutOfOfficeForSlot` returns the matching window as `data` (`packages/features/schedules/lib/slots.ts:16-25`). `IOutOfOfficeWindow` already has `start` and `end`, as ISO strings (`getUserAvailability.ts:229-232`). The slot data is built at `slots.ts:245-258`. The new fields must come only from a window, because a whole-day record has no `start`.
- The run logic is in `AvailableTimes` (`apps/web/modules/bookings/components/AvailableTimes.tsx`, in the loop after `mergeByTime`). `isAway(merged[index - 1])` is the check that joins adjacent windows. The early return for `oooAllDay` renders `slots[0]` only, which criterion 5 changes.
- `OOOSlot` passes props through to `OutOfOfficeInSlots`. `AvailableTimes` already reads `timeFormat` and `timezone` from `useBookerTime`.
- Keep the formatter a pure function with its own test file, taking the two instants, the time zone and the format. Criteria 1 to 3 then need no rendering.
- `SlotInfo` is at `packages/features/calendars/lib/types.ts:3`. The atoms have a separate `SlotInfo` (`packages/platform/atoms/booker/types.ts:112`), which this issue leaves alone.
- The new string goes in `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`, beside `ooo_user_is_ooo`.
- `getPartialDayOutOfOfficeRanges` is at `date-ranges.ts:279`, and its tests start at `date-ranges.test.ts:1297`.
- Likely files: `slots.ts`, `slots.test.ts`, `types.ts`, `AvailableTimes.tsx`, `AvailableTimes.test.tsx`, `OutOfOfficeInSlots.tsx`, the formatter and its test, `date-ranges.ts`, `date-ranges.test.ts`, and `en/common.json`.

### Requirement/Document

- Issue #104 and PR #110, Tech Debt section: https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy/pull/110
- `docs/sprint2/diagrams/104-zach-short.md`

 ## Spec Review — @dchan01-wm

Claude helped me with this; overall the spec seems good, there are a couple issues it identified (I did not extensively look into them, but you can use this as a starting point) but you should be good to go!

- **AC1:** testable, but see problem 1: on a day where every slot is away, the 12h/24h toggle is hidden, so "changing either one updates the panel" cannot be done from that day.
- **AC2:** clear and testable; the 14:10–14:50 example with 30-minute slots pins down "real times, not slot times" well.
- **AC3:** testable, but the date format is not stated (e.g. "Wed, Nov 12, 9:00pm" vs "11/12 21:00"). Please name it, or say it follows the booker's locale, so a test has an expected value that does not come from the code's own output.
- **AC4:** clear and testable, including the shorter-than-one-slot gap.
- **AC5:** clear, but interacts with problem 1 (both cases make the day "all away").
- **AC6:** clear and testable.
- **AC7:** "unbookable" is testable; "API v2 slot responses do not change" is not true as written (problem 2).
- **AC8:** testable by type-check, but incomplete (problem 3).
- **AC9:** testable, but it is a cleanup that the user story does not need (see Scope).

**Cases considered:** Covered: one window in the host's and another zone (AC1), slot-straddling edges (AC2), multi-day partial entries (AC5), back-to-back entries (AC4), whole-day entries and holidays (AC6). Overlapping entries and platform atoms are out of scope; fine.

Worth adding:
- **Window crossing the attendee's midnight:** slots are grouped by the attendee's date (`util.ts:1278`), so the panel appears on both days with the full hours. Probably right; say so in AC3 so it gets a test.
- **A booked time inside a window:** `mergeByTime` puts it between the away slots (`AvailableTimes.tsx:281-303`), splitting one window into two panels with the same hours. Pre-existing from #104; add it to Out of Scope or skip booked times in the boundary rule.
- **Embeds** also render `AvailableTimes` (`Embed.tsx:416`), so they get the hours too. Fine; worth a line.

**Scope:** Medium fits. The file list is already 10 code files plus `common.json`, and problems 1 and 3 add one or two more, which is over the 10-file PR limit (`AGENTS.md`). Suggest moving AC9 (deleting `getPartialDayOutOfOfficeRanges`, now used only by its tests: `date-ranges.ts:279`, `date-ranges.test.ts:1297-1376`) into its own small hardening issue.

**Problems found:** 

1. **12h/24h toggle hidden on all-away days.** `AvailableTimeSlots.tsx:206` and `:216` hide it when every slot is away, which conflicts with AC1 on AC5's days. Either show it when a panel has hours (add `AvailableTimeSlots.tsx` to the file list) or narrow AC1.
2. **AC7 is false for API v2 2024-04-15.** 2024-09-04 filters away slots (`slots-output.service.ts:49`, `:119`), but 2024-04-15 with no `slotFormat` and no `timeZone` returns slots unchanged (`slots-2024-04-15/services/slots-output.service.ts:25-26`), so the new fields would appear there. That is additive, so not breaking (`agents/rules/api-no-breaking-changes.md`), but the AC should say so, or the PR should strip them.
3. **AC8 misses the booker's type.** `AvailableTimes.tsx:21` uses `Slot`, which comes from `IGetAvailableSlots` (`useAvailableTimeSlots.ts:7-21`), not `SlotInfo`. Add the new fields (and `notes`) there and name the file.
4. **Name the two new fields** (e.g. `outOfOfficeStart` / `outOfOfficeEnd`).
5. Optional: `findOutOfOfficeForSlot`'s return type (`slots.ts:13`, `:20`) has no `start`/`end` and needs widening.

Everything else in the technical notes matches the code (`slots.ts:16-25`, `:245-258`; `getUserAvailability.ts:229-232`; `AvailableTimes.tsx:272-306`; `util.ts:1275-1290`; `outOfOfficeCreateOrUpdate.handler.ts:152-161`). The design is feasible, and both decisions have two well-argued alternatives.

@@ -0,0 +1,35 @@
+import dayjs from "@calcom/dayjs";
+
+type AwaySlot = { away?: boolean; outOfOfficeStart?: string };
+
+/**
+ * The start and end of an out-of-office window as the booker reads them: in the booker's time zone and
+ * 12-hour or 24-hour format. When the two instants fall on different dates in that zone, each one gets its
+ * date, written the way the booker's locale writes it.
+ */
+export function formatAwayWindow(
+  startIso: string,
+  endIso: string,
+  timeZone: string,
+  timeFormat: string,
+  locale?: string
+): { start: string; end: string } {
+  // Day.js is used because the result depends on the zone's offset at each instant, which changes on a DST day.
+  const start = dayjs.utc(startIso).tz(timeZone);
+  const end = dayjs.utc(endIso).tz(timeZone);
+
+  if (start.format("YYYY-MM-DD") === end.format("YYYY-MM-DD")) {
+    return { start: start.format(timeFormat), end: end.format(timeFormat) };
+  }
+
+  const date = new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { month: "short", day: "numeric", timeZone });
+  return {
+    start: `${date.format(start.toDate())}, ${start.format(timeFormat)}`,
+    end: `${date.format(end.toDate())}, ${end.format(timeFormat)}`,
+  };
+}
+
+/** A day prints no clock time when every slot is away and no away panel has hours, as for a whole-day entry. */
+export function dayPrintsNoTimes(slots: AwaySlot[]): boolean {
+  return slots.length > 0 && slots.every((slot) => slot.away && !slot.outOfOfficeStart);
+}

+// Mutation testing for Sprint 3 (D6). Run it on the files your PR changed, never on the whole repo:
+//   TZ=UTC yarn stryker run --mutate "path/to/file.ts"
+// Set STRYKER_JSON to write the JSON report where the course wants it, for example
+//   STRYKER_JSON=docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/130-zach-short-before.json
+/** @type {import("@stryker-mutator/api/core").PartialStrykerOptions} */
+export default {
+  testRunner: "vitest",
+  plugins: ["@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner"],
+  vitest: {
+    configFile: "vitest.config.mts",
+    // Only the tests that import the mutated file run, which keeps a run to minutes in this monorepo.
+    related: true,
+  },
+  // Not inPlace: in this repo the in-place backup lands inside the project, Vitest then collects the backup
+  // copies, and the restore drops the executable bit on scripts. The sandbox copy avoids both. These folders
+  // have no unit tests that features or web code import, so leaving them out keeps the copy small.
+  // .claude and .cursor hold symlinks to folders, and packages/prisma/.env links to a root .env that may not
+  // exist; the sandbox copy fails on all three.
+  ignorePatterns: [
+    "docs",
+    "ai-logs",
+    "specs",
+    "apps/api/v2",
+    "apps/web/public",
+    "packages/embeds",
+    "reports",
+    ".claude",
+    ".cursor",
+    "packages/prisma/.env",
+  ],
+  ignoreStatic: true,
+  concurrency: 4,
+  timeoutMS: 30000,
+  reporters: ["clear-text", "progress", "json", "html"],
+  jsonReporter: { fileName: process.env.STRYKER_JSON ?? "reports/mutation/mutation.json" },
+  htmlReporter: { fileName: "reports/mutation/mutation.html" },
+};

export const AvailableTimes = ({
  slots,
  showTimeFormatToggle = true,
  className,
  date,
  bookedTimes = [],
  ...props
}: AvailableTimesProps) => {
  const { t } = useLocale();
  const { timeFormat, timezone } = useBookerTime();

  // Two entries can touch, so a run of away slots is one panel only while the window stays the same. Slots of
  // a whole-day entry have no window, so they all compare equal.
  const inSamePanel = (slot: Slot, other: Slot | string | undefined) =>
    typeof other === "object" &&
    !!other.away &&
    other.outOfOfficeStart === slot.outOfOfficeStart &&
    other.outOfOfficeEnd === slot.outOfOfficeEnd;

  const oooAllDay = slots.length > 0 && slots.every((slot) => inSamePanel(slots[0], slot));
  if (oooAllDay) {
    return <OOOSlot {...slots[0]} />;
  }

  // A partial-day entry leaves a run of away slots in the middle of the day. One panel stands in for each run,
  // at the first away slot, so the panel sits between the slots before and after the window.
  const merged = mergeByTime(slots, date ? bookedTimes : []);
  const items: ReactNode[] = [];
  for (let index = 0; index < merged.length; index++) {
    const slot = merged[index];
    if (typeof slot === "string") {
      items.push(
        <JoinWaitlistButton
          key={slot}
          date={date ?? ""}
          slotStart={slot}
          label={t("waitlist_join_time", { time: dayjs.utc(slot).tz(timezone).format(timeFormat) })}
        />
      );
      continue;
    }
    if (!slot.away) {
      items.push(<SlotItem key={slot.time} slot={slot} {...props} />);
      continue;
    }
    if (inSamePanel(slot, merged[index - 1])) continue;
    let runEnd = index;
    while (inSamePanel(slot, merged[runEnd + 1])) runEnd++;
    items.push(
      <OOOSlot key={`ooo-${slot.time}`} {...slot} className={runEnd === merged.length - 1 ? "pb-0" : ""} />
    );
  }

  return (
    <div className={classNames("text-default flex flex-col", className)}>
      <div className="h-full pb-4">
        {!slots.length && (
          <div
            data-testId="no-slots-available"
            className="bg-subtle border-subtle flex h-full flex-col items-center rounded-md border p-6 dark:bg-transparent">
            <CalendarX2Icon className="text-muted mb-2 h-4 w-4" />
            <p className={classNames("text-muted", showTimeFormatToggle ? "-mt-1 text-lg" : "text-sm")}>
              {t("all_booked_today")}
            </p>
            {date && bookedTimes.length > 0 && (
              <JoinWaitlistButton date={date} label={t("waitlist_join_day")} className="mb-0 mt-4" />
            )}

import { useBookerStoreContext } from "@calcom/features/bookings/Booker/BookerStoreProvider";
import { getBookerTimezone } from "@calcom/features/bookings/Booker/utils/getBookerTimezone";
import { useTimePreferences } from "@calcom/features/bookings/lib/timePreferences";
import { shallow } from "zustand/shallow";

export const useBookerTime = () => {
  const [timezoneFromBookerStore] = useBookerStoreContext((state) => [state.timezone], shallow);
  const { timezone: timezoneFromTimePreferences, timeFormat } = useTimePreferences();
  const timezone = getBookerTimezone({
    storeTimezone: timezoneFromBookerStore,
    bookerUserPreferredTimezone: timezoneFromTimePreferences,
  });

  return {
    timezone,
    timeFormat,
    timezoneFromBookerStore,
    timezoneFromTimePreferences,
  };
};

import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { dayPrintsNoTimes, formatAwayWindow } from "./formatAwayWindow";

const TWELVE_HOUR = "h:mma";
const TWENTY_FOUR_HOUR = "HH:mm";

// Every expected value below is worked out by hand from the UTC offset of the zone on that date.
describe("formatAwayWindow", () => {
  describe("a window that starts and ends on one date", () => {
    // A London host is away 14:00 to 15:00 on 2026-10-08. London is on BST (UTC+1), so that is 13:00Z to 14:00Z.
    const start = "2026-10-08T13:00:00.000Z";
    const end = "2026-10-08T14:00:00.000Z";

    it("shows the hours in the attendee's zone, not the host's", () => {
      // New York is on EDT (UTC-4).
      expect(formatAwayWindow(start, end, "America/New_York", TWELVE_HOUR, "en")).toEqual({
        start: "9:00am",
        end: "10:00am",
      });
    });

    it("shows the host's own hours when the attendee is in the host's zone", () => {
      expect(formatAwayWindow(start, end, "Europe/London", TWENTY_FOUR_HOUR, "en")).toEqual({
        start: "14:00",
        end: "15:00",
      });
    });

    it("follows the 12-hour or 24-hour format for the same zone", () => {
      expect(formatAwayWindow(start, end, "America/New_York", TWENTY_FOUR_HOUR, "en")).toEqual({
        start: "09:00",
        end: "10:00",
      });
      expect(formatAwayWindow(start, end, "Europe/London", TWELVE_HOUR, "en")).toEqual({
        start: "2:00pm",
        end: "3:00pm",
      });
    });

    it("shows the minutes of the window, not a rounded slot time", () => {
      expect(
        formatAwayWindow(
          "2026-10-08T14:10:00.000Z",
          "2026-10-08T14:50:00.000Z",
          "UTC",
          TWENTY_FOUR_HOUR,
          "en"
        )
      ).toEqual({ start: "14:10", end: "14:50" });
    });

    it("uses a zone with a half-hour offset", () => {
      // Kolkata is UTC+5:30 all year.
      expect(formatAwayWindow(start, end, "Asia/Kolkata", TWENTY_FOUR_HOUR, "en")).toEqual({
        start: "18:30",
        end: "19:30",
      });
    });
  });

I've reviewed PR #153 (Zach Short's, closes #130) and drafted the rubric. The code looks correct, but the PR can't merge yet: as of a few minutes ago it conflicts with main. Your rubric is in `.claude/work/pr-153/review.md`, with Notes filled in, Scores blank, and the template wording checked.

## What the PR does
For a partial-day out-of-office entry, the away panel on the booking page now shows the hours ("Away 9:00am to 10:00am"). The times follow the visitor's chosen time zone and 12h/24h setting. It also fixes an older bug: two entries back to back used to show one panel, with only the first entry's note and redirect. They now show one panel each.

**The parts it touches:**
- **Slot engine** (`packages/features/schedules/lib/slots.ts:260-264`): when it marks a slot as away, it now also copies the entry's start and end onto the slot. This only happens for partial-day entries. Whole-day entries get neither field. Confirmed: the per-date summary record and whole-day records carry no start time (`getUserAvailability.ts:249-256`, `:841`), and only the per-window records do (`:828-832`).
- **Shared types** (`types.ts`, `useAvailableTimeSlots.ts`): the two fields and `notes` are optional additions.
- **Booking page** (`AvailableTimes.tsx:275-314`): a new panel starts wherever the entry changes, so back-to-back entries split. Whole-day slots have no hours on any of them, so they still form one panel (Confirmed).
- **New formatter** (`formatAwayWindow.ts`): turns the start and end into the display text, adding the date when they fall on different days.
- **12h/24h toggle** (`AvailableTimeSlots.tsx:208`): it's now hidden only on days whose panel shows no hours. This fixes problem 1 from your spec review.

### D2 — Requirements specification (individual, 20 pts)

- [ ] Same format as Sprint 1: user story meeting INVEST, user scenario, at least 3 testable acceptance criteria, out of scope, open questions
- [ ] Hardening issues fixing a defect use the bug format (OB, EB, S2R, other details); other hardening issues use the short task format (problem, goal, acceptance criteria, other details)
- [ ] Spec written and reviewed before coding: a teammate posts a spec review comment on the issue saying what was checked (template 11)
- [ ] Review teammates' specs the same way

### D3 — Design decisions (individual, 5 pts)

- [ ] At least one non-trivial decision per issue, with Decision, Alternatives (2+ concrete), Rationale, Consequences

### D4 — Code changes and PRs (individual, 20 pts)

- [ ] Same workflow as Sprint 2 (branch per issue, tests for every behavioral change)
- [ ] PR description: `Closes #N`, what/why, `## Test Evidence` (replaces "how it was tested"), `## Tech Debt`
- [ ] Test Evidence: one row per acceptance criterion (bug reports: the Expected Behavior; no product behavior change: "N/A" and why); source of expected value is `AC`, `issue discussion`, `docs`, `upstream behavior`, or `other` (explain) — never the current output of your own code
- [ ] Hardening issues include evidence the problem is fixed (bug fix: a test that fails before and passes after; flaky test: root cause and repeated runs before/after, e.g. 20 unit or 10 E2E; CI check: links to runs before/after; baseline failures: pass/fail counts before/after and the cause of each group)
- [ ] If the fork has no CI running your tests, include the commands you ran and a results summary (passed, failed, skipped)
- [ ] Request review on GitHub and notify on Zulip; merge only after an approval on the latest commit
